core.verify.note: client-core's verifier, which the Node runner drives vector for vector and the browser runner (conformance/runners/browser, the same suites) drives in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, through WebCrypto's Ed25519.

core.cache.note: SP-R02: bearer mode keeps a verified CacheRecordV3 in IndexedDB (signed artifacts only: the trust manifest and both documents, ETags, the unsigned hints that only tighten the gate), re-verified against the pins on every load (src/browser/bearer/session.ts); the sync-etag-304 transcript replays through it. On desktop the host's Node SDK holds the cache and the renderer reads it through the bridge.

core.bundle.note: Desktop through the Node Electron bridge (protocol v4 importBundle); browser verified in-page by client-core inspectBundle against a random device id kept in IndexedDB. The browser runner drives inspectBundle over every bundleCases vector in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

core.local.note: SP-15: localAdapter() (@polaris-key/react/local) serves the documents the build bundles and a fixed licence state with no fetch in reach: it takes no transport, and every verb that would dial rejects local-only. The gate, config, config.local, crash tags, the boot guard and boot() work offline; supports() answers runtime N/A for the rest. A test with a throwing fetch stub proves no call is made.

except.note: On desktop the host process's store holds the token.

core.store.note: SP-R02: bearer mode's indexedDbStore (src/browser/bearer/store.ts) implements client-core's Store: the token in its own object store, the random device id and the cache in the offline record; status() reports backend indexeddb, degraded not-persistent unless navigator.storage.persisted(). A page without trust.pinnedKeys holds no credential, so its supports() answers it runtime-unsupported. Device binding to a hardware anchor is a typed N/A in a browser: the device id is a random value in IndexedDB and there is no platform anchor to re-derive it from; on desktop the host's Node SDK binds it.

core.copy.note: English is src/copy.generated.ts (pnpm gen constants, from conformance/parity/copy.en.json): copyMessage/copyTitle read the error-code, gate and activation tables, describeError reads a typed activation result from the activation table only. French is the hand-written proof locale until SP-03.

core.backend.note: A page without trust.pinnedKeys holds no signed licence document, so its supports() says runtime, with the reason in detail. usePolarisFetch() over adapter.backendHeaders(): same origin by default (HTTPS or loopback) plus config.backend.origins; the freshness pre-sync, one retry on license_stale/license_invalid, typed not_entitled/sign_in_required; redirects refused unless asked for. Desktop: the host's client.backend.headers() through bridge v4 invoke core.backendHeaders. test/backend.test.ts replays backend-matrix.json's client rows.

except.note: On desktop the host's Node SDK enrols.

license.enroll.note:
SP-R02: bearer mode's POST /

/license/enroll, then a sync (adapter.enroll()); activate-enroll-deactivate replays through it.

license.manage.note: PX-W8: the device-limit result exposes manageUrl (validated), plus the return and key helpers.

except.note: On desktop the host's Node SDK re-registers inside its own sync (P1b-06); test/bridge.test.ts pins the renderer picking up the host's post-re-register state.

license.reregister.note: SP-R02: bearer mode's single re-acquire takes devices/register for a registered (or licence-less) device, as Node's chooseReacquireRoute; register-reregister-401 replays through it.

license.refusals.note: src/core/activation.ts classifyActivation maps every refusal by its body code (never a collapsed 403); bearer mode's activate/enroll return it and activate-refusals replays through BearerSession. The desktop bridge classifies through the same table.

config.secret.note: New desktop-bridge N/A (P1b-01). The desktop renderer never holds secrets either; the host reads them with the Node SDK.

config.mint.note:
SP-R02: bearer mode's GET /

/config/mint//token, memory-cached per device token until 30 s before expiry (edge-mint replays through it). Desktop: bridge v4's invoke("config", "mint", {recipeId}) forwards to the Node Electron host's client.config.mintToken() and answers {token, expiresAt}; a v3 host is refused typed (reason version).

config.mirror.note: The TypeScript mirror is rendered by tools/gen-mirrors.ts.

config.local.note: adapter.config.set/clear/clearAll/setting/onConfigChange (SP-13): validated against the catalog type, refused for an admin-managed key, a change event per resolved-value move. Browser: localStorage per product, a memory fallback reported by config.persistent(). Desktop: forwarded to the host's client.config over bridge v4 (a v3 host is refused typed, reason version). useConfigSetting(key) re-renders on change. test/configLocal.test.tsx.

config.sync.note: U-20: adapter.config.setting(key).sync() and useSetting(key).sync over the browser Cloud Sync host (src/browser/cloudSync); test/cloudSyncSettings.test.tsx. A page without pinned keys, the local adapter and the desktop bridge answer the typed N/A (the host serves no Cloud Sync verb on bridge v4, D-6).

devices.fingerprint.note: New desktop-bridge N/A (P1b-01). On desktop the host's Node SDK computes it.

devices.facts.note: New desktop-bridge N/A (P1b-01). On desktop the host's Node SDK collects them.

except.note: On desktop the host's Node SDK registers.

devices.register.note: SP-R02: bearer mode registers keylessly at load when discovery's core.registration is open (autoRegister), or on adapter.register(); register-open replays through it.

devices.manage.note:
Desktop through the bridge's invoke("devices", …). Web in bearer mode (SP-R02): GET /

/devices, PATCH and DELETE /

/devices/:id with the device token. A page without trust.pinnedKeys holds no device bearer and refuses with invalid-options.

devices.report.note:
Desktop through invoke("devices", "report"). Web in bearer mode (SP-R02): POST /

/devices/report after every sync and on report(), with the browser facts (os family, cores, memory bucket, locale, time zone), caps, outlet and the update-health journal (src/browser/bearer/facts.ts); telemetry-report replays through it. A page without trust.pinnedKeys refuses with invalid-options.

telemetry.updates.note:
adapter.recordUpdateEvent(event, input) journals a P6-03 event with Node's defaults and validation (src/core/updateEvents.ts). Web in bearer mode (SP-R02): BearerSession's in-page journal, drained at most 16 per POST /

/devices/report and dropped only on a 200; decideUpdate() journals update_offered once per offered release; telemetry-report-updates replays through recorded events. identity.devicecode.note:
Desktop through the bridge (beginSignIn/pollSignIn, v4 adds the expiry, interval and identity). Web in bearer mode (SP-R02): POST /

/identity/auth/device/{start,poll} through adapter.beginSignIn(); devicecode-happy and devicecode-expired replay through it.

identity.devicelabel.note: PX-W13: a browser has no platform device name, so by default it reports none (the card shows the registered origin); in bearer mode a host may name one (browserAdapter deviceName, or per call on beginSignIn), sent on registration, activation and sign-in. Through the desktop bridge the main process's Node SDK sends it; the corpus runs through client-core's normalizeDeviceLabel.

identity.toggle.note: I-10a.10: signIn.start on a product that does not run Identity (the adapter's capability map, or the Worker's 404 on the device start) is the typed UnsupportedError service-unavailable, before any other request; licences keep working.

identity.attach.note: I-10a.9: bearer mode over the identity fragment discovery names (subject, signout, attach); the desktop bridge through invoke("identity", …) on a v4 host (typed version N/A otherwise). A page without trust.pinnedKeys refuses with invalid-options.

identity.account.note: I-10a.9: bearer mode over the identity fragment discovery names (subject, signout, attach); the desktop bridge through invoke("identity", …) on a v4 host (typed version N/A otherwise). A page without trust.pinnedKeys refuses with invalid-options.

identity.redirect.web.note: I-10a.10: bearer mode. signIn.start({channel: "redirect", redirectUri}) builds the PKCE authorize URL with client-core and keeps the verifier and state in sessionStorage keyed by state; signIn.complete(callbackUrl) (or the session's) checks state and iss and redeems the code at the token endpoint. The desktop renderer signs in by device code only: its redirect is a typed unsupported (runtime) since the bridge has no verb to redeem a code in the host. Cookie mode is removed (SP-40).

identity.choice.note: I-10a.11: bearer mode: usePolarisAuth().choice.{licenses, devices, complete, cancel} over the choice endpoints discovery names, a refusal being a result; useLicenseChoice(grant) is the hook. On the desktop, bridge v6 (UK-42.22.7) runs the same four calls over invoke(identity, choice.*) with an opaque ref the host bound to the window, the Worker's grant staying in the host; a host below v6 answers the typed unsupported (version). A page without trust.pinnedKeys refuses with invalid-options.

identity.devicecode.choice.note: UK-42.22.5: beginSignIn sends licenseChoice app only when discovery has deviceChoice and the four choice* endpoints; pollSignIn and waitForSignIn answer status choose (grant, choices, expiresIn) and the device-code session's wait() settles kind choose with no token. The desktop bridge (UK-42.22.7, protocol v6) answers choose from pollSignIn with an opaque ref; below v6 licenseChoice app is the typed unsupported (version) and discovery reads without deviceChoice.

identity.signin.hints.note: I-10a.10: bearer mode: loginHint, nameHint and purpose go on the authorize URL (redirect) and the device start body (device code). UK-42.17: the desktop bridge's beginSignIn carries loginHint, nameHint, purpose "attach" and licenseChoice to the host's Node sign-in, validated on both sides; only scope is a typed unsupported (runtime).

identity.keyreturn.note: LK-SKIP.6b: bearer mode. signIn.start({channel: "redirect", redirectUri, keyReturn: true}) appends key_return=allow and signIn.complete settles an activated outcome (the key's license, subject null, keyEntries) for a via: "key" answer, stored as a key activation. The kits start the app at once (no ActivateDone; AccountAndLicense shows Not in an account from the license's profile). A token refusal (device_limit, key_entry_limit, license_owned) carries the typed activation with limit, deviceCount, manageUrl and keyEntries and opens the key step. Both redirect-web-key-return transcripts replay. The desktop renderer signs in by device code only, so its redirect is the same typed unsupported (runtime) as identity.redirect.web.

except.note: A browser signs in by identity.redirect.web; it has no loopback listener or registered scheme, and signIn.start({channel: "redirect"}) with no redirectUri answers the typed runtime unsupported.

identity.redirect.native.note: I-15b.8: on the desktop, signIn.start({channel: "redirect"}) with no redirectUri forwards to the Node host over the v6 bridge (beginSignIn({channel: "redirect"}); the host binds the listener, opens the browser and redeems the code, the renderer holds a flow id). The session polls pollSignIn like the device-code one; reopen() asks the host to open the browser page again, cancel() stops waiting here (the host ends the flow on its next begin, sign-out, window close or expiry). A bridge below v6 is the typed version unsupported. Proof is the host's replay of the redirect-native-* transcripts (sdk-node) plus test/desktopNativeRedirect.test.ts.

except.note: The desktop renderer holds no device key; the host's Node SDK would sign in.

identity.exchange.note: I-46.3, I-46.5: bearer mode: session.exchange(port, {kind, subjectToken}) posts the device's keys for a nonce, takes the provider's token for it and the RFC 8693 grant with the exchange proof; an answer is an outcome (signedIn, pendingConsent, pendingSignIn, needsSignIn, unavailable) and a refusal a typed PolarisError. All eight exchange-* and discovery-identity-exchange transcripts replay through it over a fixture key port.

identity.gamecenter.note: Game Center exists only on Apple platforms.

identity.pgs.note: Play Games runs only on Android.

identity.autosignin.note: I-46: usePolarisAuth().autoSignIn() runs the ladder (a stored token, the provider silently through FedCM, its chooser only with prompt optional); a result, never a throw. The gate runs it once at boot and Provider autoSignIn={false} turns it off. A local adapter holds no platform sign-in and answers unavailable (runtime). On the desktop bridge (v5, I-47b) the host runs the stored-token rung and answers signedIn or needsSignIn; a v4 host answers unavailable (runtime); the gate stays on Welcome. test/autoSignIn.test.ts runs it against a scripted Worker.

identity.restore.note: A browser has no platform backup item and the desktop renderer holds no device key (I-49).

except.note: The desktop renderer holds no device key; the adapter has no `link`, and the kit shows no offer.

identity.link.note: I-46.13: `link.offer()`, `accept()` (the held handle, else one provider prompt), `decline()` (sha256(issuer ‖ sub) in IndexedDB), lazy after a redirect sign-in; the kit's link-offer, link-done and link-conflict steps over the app. Replays I-43.3's link-* transcripts.

except.note: No mode v handshake in a browser tab, and the page holds no device key (I-40).

identity.nearby.note: I-47b: on the desktop bridge (v5) the host plays either device. adapter.nearby.request() is the new device (D) and adapter.nearby.approver() the signed-in one (M); the kit draws them as <NearbySignIn> and <NearbyApproval>. The renderer holds an ask id, never a request id, key or token. A v4 host answers the typed unsupported (reason version). UXR-47b: every ending of a request draws its own screen (Try again, Use a code instead), several approvers are listed, the approver has a screen of its own and says when it stopped. test/desktopAdapter.test.ts, test/kitNearby.test.tsx and test/kitNearbyFix.test.tsx.

identity.keyentry.note: I-10a.9: activateWithKey resolves with keyEntries; key_entry_limit (manageUrl, keyEntries) and license_owned (signInUrl) are typed activation outcomes that keep the token, cache and store. Desktop through submitKey's BridgeActivation.

release.record.note: client-core verifyReleaseRecord (hash before signature, pinned release keys only); the browser adapter fetches by hash and persists releaseRecords in IndexedDB, desktop through the host's decide().

release.fetch.note: adapter.releaseFetch(target): discovery builds route, the bearer session's device bearer and X-PKey-* headers, held bytes resumed with Range and If-Range on the payload SHA-256, size and SHA-256 checked against the verified record before a Blob is returned; a refusal is release-refused with the server code; on desktop-bridge the host's client.release.fetch() over bridge v4 (SP-12).

release.distribution.note:
adapter.downloadModel() and thisPlatform(): the public GET /

/distribution/download.json with no credential, the visitor's platform from the user agent; on desktop-bridge the host's client.distribution over bridge v4 (SP-12).

update.feed.note: client-core verifyFeed with floors keyed by the canonical channel; the browser adapter fetches, verifies and persists the feeds slice in IndexedDB; desktop through invoke("update", "decide").

update.feeds.note: adapter.feedUrl(kind) on desktop-bridge: the host's client.update.feedUrl() over bridge v4, the typed version N/A on an older host; the web adapter answers the runtime N/A (SP-12).

except.note: A browser has no native updater feed; the service worker is update.driver.

update.decide.note: client-core decideUpdate/runUpdateCheck on both adapters (test/updateDecision.test.ts, test/updateMatrixParity.test.ts); useUpdateDecision hands the host the decision and whether it is undismissable, for its own prompt. The browser outlet is web unless the host passes one.

update.content.note: client-core decideUpdate with content; useUpdateDecision exposes the content reason (revoked-content stops the boot, content-floor prompts) and the boot value. The Node and browser runners drive every contentRows and feedContentCases vector.

update.driver.note: SP-15: adapter.installUpdate(decision) answers an InstallOutcome. Web: a platform decision hands off to the registration's waiting service worker (postMessage SKIP_WAITING, wait for control, reload) and answers handedOff, restartRequired with reload: false, or unsupported{reason} with no worker; binary and store decisions are runtime N/A. Desktop-bridge: forwarded to the host's client.update.install() over bridge v4 (invoke update.install), the typed version N/A on an older host. update_downloaded and update_applied go through recordUpdateEvent.

update.bootguard.note: SP-15: markBootAttempt() and confirmBoot() over client-core's bootGuardAction. Web: slots (current, previous, failedBoots, confirmed, skipVersion) in localStorage with a memory fallback, a waiting service worker counted as staged, an optional host rollback, update_confirmed/update_reverted/boot_rolled_back through recordUpdateEvent; boot() runs it as its guard stage and confirms per bootConfirmation. Desktop-bridge: the host's guard over bridge v4 (invoke update.markBootAttempt / update.confirmBoot). The guardCases and confirmCases of stage-matrix.json replay against persisted slots.

outlet.detect.note: client-core's detectOutlet, re-exported; the browser adapter reads the page's display mode (readOutletSignals) and detects over the synthesised web stamp when the host names no outlet. The desktop adapter defers to the host (Node's detection).

crash.tags.note: adapter.crashTags() / crashTagsFor(): release <deliverable>@<version>[+<build>], environment the channel, pkey.outlet the resolved outlet, as the Worker Sentry hook parses them; on desktop-bridge the host's client.crashTags() over bridge v4 (SP-12).

packs.record.note: client-core verifyReleaseRecord with pin.kind and verifyMarker; the Node and Chromium runners drive every packRecordCases and markerCases vector.

packs.revoke.note: client-core verifyRevocation, newerRevocation and the PackEngine's revocations.json; the Node and browser runners drive every revocationCases vector.

packs.delegation.note: client-core verifyReleaseRecord (the delegated path), verifyDelegation, recordRevoked and dataOnlyRefusal through the shared PackEngine; the Node and browser runners drive every delegationCases and dataOnlyCases vector.

packs.plan.note: client-core plan, selectVariant and planTarget; every plan-matrix.json row and case in the Node and Chromium runners.

packs.index.files.note: client-core parseFilesIndex, checkPaths and treeDigest; filesIndexCases in Chromium through @polaris-key/zstd-wasm's browser entry.

packs.index.chunks.note: client-core parseChunkIndex; all 22 chunkIndexCases in Chromium through @polaris-key/zstd-wasm's browser entry; the OPFS store keeps seed indexes under <packs>/index/<sha256>.

packs.apply.full.note: client-core applyFull; applyCases in Chromium under the WASM decoder. P4-18: a container's full goes first through the payload URL (Content-Encoding: zstd, decoded by the browser, kept as a dictionary), written by the OPFS worker, size and SHA-256 checked against the record; then the blob route and WASM.

packs.apply.file.note: client-core applyFile with the type-neutral container rebuild; applyCases in Chromium under the WASM decoder.

packs.apply.chunk.note: client-core applyChunk over the OPFS store (a write-behind container output read back for duplicates, repair and resume; staging/<planId>/journal.json), single-range requests with If-Range; the 8 chunk applyCases in Chromium under the WASM decoder; chunk is in caps.strategies.

packs.apply.delta.note: @polaris-key/zstd-wasm's browser entry (wasm32, P = 30, memBudget at most 2^30); the window check runs in the applier. P4-18: a planned payload delta runs first as Compression Dictionary Transport (the target's payload URL with ?via=dcz; Content-Encoding: dcz, the artifact plus 40 bytes, applied by Chromium), output SHA-256 checked against the record; a 409 (no dictionary: evicted, chunk-assembled base, Firefox, Safari) or a failure falls back to the WASM delta, then the plan's remaining candidates. Never for a gated pack or a base over 100 MiB.

packs.delta.feed.note: client-core's reader, merge and one-feed-delta rule (as Node); browserPacks wires feedDeltas to the committed feed, and the desktop bridge runs the Node engine. On the web, P4-18's payload URL answers dcz from a lazy delta's base; without it the WASM delta runs through the blob route.

packs.state.note: createBrowserPacks (update.packs) over client-core's PackEngine: OPFS staging and store (or an explicit in-memory store), journal, Range/If-Range resume, re-verified reload, confirm, rollback, GC roots; packSetId() for the host (a browser cannot post devices/report).

packs.handlers.note: update.packs.registerHandler; files.tree, data.json and l10n.table built in; check(staged) refuses a staged payload with pack-type-check-failed before it commits (P4-16); custom.<name> through registerHandler.

packs.type.godot.zip.note: P4-16: a godot.zip is mounted only by Godot's load_resource_pack.

packs.type.l10n.table.note: P4-16: L10nTableHandler, built in: PO, CSV or JSON tables parsed by plain parsers (never evaluated), each table's BCP-47 locale matched to the variant's locale axis; hot; tables(packId) and onActivate/onDeactivate.

packs.type.data.json.note: P4-16: DataJsonHandler, built in: every file strict JSON with an object at the top, whatever its name; formatVersions the host lists (default [1]); hot; documents(packId) and onActivate/onDeactivate.

packs.type.audio.bank.note: P4-16: audio banks load through a game engine's middleware.

packs.type.ml.model.note: P4-16: MlModelHandler, registered by the host with its runtimes, RAM/VRAM budget, quantisations and load test: model.json checked, the staged file load-tested, then model(packId) swaps; hot.

sync.scenarios.note: conformance/runners/browser/syncScenarios.browser.test.ts drives every sync-scenarios.json scenario (the count equals the corpus's) and settingCases in a real engine through client-core's cloud-sync machine, which the browser host runs; conformance/runners/node/syncScenarios.test.ts is the same driver on Node.

sync.settings.note: U-20.3: config.set routed through the browser Cloud Sync machine while a person is signed in, setting(key).sync(), the onConfigChange origin, the one-time import, the pre-sign-out flush, the sign-in offer; useSetting and useCloudSync. The 17 cloudsync-* transcripts replay through it (test/transcripts.test.ts); test/cloudSyncSettings.test.tsx and cloudSyncHost.test.ts. A page without pinned keys, the local adapter and the desktop bridge answer the typed N/A (the host serves no Cloud Sync verb on bridge v4, D-6).

sync.conflict.note: useConflicts() (src/react/useConflicts.ts) and adapter.cloudSync.onConflict/conflicts/cloudEmpty over the browser host's MergeRegistry (ui-core browser/cloudSync): a revision put the server refuses opens one MergeRequest, the device keeps its copy unsent until keep, and conflictOpened/conflictClosed ride onEvents; useCloudSync().cloudEmpty and status.conflicts. Only the writer tab keeps a request. Save writes open the same requests. Replays sync-scenarios.json v5 in the browser runner with no skip. test/useConflicts.test.tsx, test/cloudSyncSaves.test.ts, test/kitSaveBind.test.tsx.

sync.saves.note: SAVES.R (U-22.7): useSaves() and useTransfers() over adapter.cloudSync.saves, the browser host's SavesApi (loaded on the first call, lazySaves). It binds client-core's SavesClient to the machine's records, putAt, removeAt and onOutcome (MachineRecords, as Node and Python) and to createBrowserFiles; every engine entry runs under the Web Lock, so two tabs never drive one journal. The keyring's file codec goes through withRoot and refuses with sync-locked on every method and stream piece once the ring locks. Sign-out and forget: lock the ring, purge the saves (running writes, journal, chunk cache; the files layer is closed so a running transfer cannot recreate the database), then drop the pin. cancel() settles the waiting write as cancelled; the wait for the metadata write has no timeout. Only the writer tab owns a live machine: write and delete from another tab reject with sync-not-writer; list, read and revisions work in every tab. cloudsync-files-single replays in test/transcripts.test.ts; test/cloudSyncSaves.test.ts drives write, read, conflict, resolve, delete, cancel, the locked codec and the purge order. A page without pinned keys, the local adapter and the desktop bridge answer the typed N/A.

sync.keyring.note: U-38.2: the browser bearer engine's key ring (RingEngine, ui-core browser/ring) on client-core's sync crypto and WebCrypto. The seven keyring-* transcripts replay through it (test/transcripts.test.ts); test/keyring.test.ts pins create, unwrap of this device's wrap, wrap to another device, recover and set the recovery code, reset and adopt, the lock and the codec keys. The root is a non-extractable HKDF key in IndexedDB; its bytes live in memory for 300 s after a create or recovery. A browser unlocks only with the recovery code (Q8). A browser whose device keys are memory-only (WebKit) cannot create or reset a ring (the Worker needs registered keys): it unlocks with the code and keeps the root in memory, so every load asks for the code again. A page without pinned keys, the local adapter and the desktop bridge answer the typed N/A (runtime, runtime, version): the host serves no ring verb yet.

sync.records.note: U-46 (C26.3R): adapter.cloudSync.collection(name) and useCollection(name) over client-core's SyncCollection and the browser host's machine (src/browser/cloudSync/collection.ts). The catalog's collections (exact names and prefix.* patterns) reach the machine; the hook loads the handle, re-renders on its change events and exposes ids, get(id) and the handle's verbs (put with ifVersion, update, add, remove, delete, on); a refusal is returned and nothing is sent. The machine is read at each call, and a rebuild keeps the watched collections and outcome taps. Only the writer tab writes: another tab's write verb throws sync-not-writer. A page without pinned keys, the local adapter and the desktop bridge answer the typed N/A (feature sync.records). test/cloudSyncCollection.test.tsx; the seven cloudsync-records-* transcripts replay in test/transcripts.test.ts.

sync.files.note:
U-22.6: the file layer of the browser host, not yet the saves API (sync.saves waits on U-22.5's machine change). BrowserFileTransport (the closed route list, no redirect, Content-Digest, bounded bodies), the IndexedDB journal and LRU chunk cache in pkey-sync-

-files (deleted with the person), client-core's TransferEngine over them with Retry-After waited out up to 3600 s, one writer by the Web Lock pkey-sync-files: (createBrowserFiles, loaded on demand). The cloudsync-files-* transcripts replay through the transport (test/transcripts.test.ts); test/cloudSyncFiles.browser.test.ts drives the engine, the journal and the lock. cloudsync-files-single is also tagged sync.saves and replays with it. A page without pinned keys, the local adapter and the desktop bridge hold no files (the typed N/A comes with the saves API).

sync.files.delta.note: U-22.6: the chunks mode of the same transport and engine (plan, put chunk, manifest, GET chunk). The cloudsync-chunks and cloudsync-chunks-delta transcripts replay through the transport; sync-vectors.json cdcCases run in the browser runner. A chunk the Worker stored with zstd (codec 1) is refused as sync-file-invalid: the browser carries no zstd decoder, and every writer emits raw chunks (D-4).

sync.e2e.recovery.note: The recovery code in the browser bearer engine's key ring (ui-core browser/ring): useRecoveryCode()'s unlock(code), replace() and reset() (create() returns the first code), and the kit's UnlockSync, RecoveryCode and RingChange screens over it. test/keyring.test.ts (the recovery code, start over, the pin), test/kitSyncScreens.test.tsx (UnlockSync, RecoveryCode, RingChange and the locked CloudSyncStatus row) and the recoveryCodeCases of sync-vectors.json in conformance/runners/browser/syncVectors.browser.test.ts; keyring-recovery replays in test/transcripts.test.ts. A browser has no platform backup API, so the code is its only backup (the registry's web allowance). A page without pinned keys, the local adapter and the desktop bridge answer the typed N/A, as for sync.keyring.

sync.e2e.note: The browser host seals and opens every synced value through client-core's sync crypto over WebCrypto (encryption defaults to e2e; the cloudSync.encryption adapter option is app code only, never read from the Worker) and the page's key ring. syncScenarios.browser.test.ts replays every e2e scenario, e2e-conflict-plaintext-copy-refused included; syncVectors.browser.test.ts the vectors; test/cloudSyncHost.test.ts the host.

connect.identity.note: CC-09.1: adapter.connect (ui-core browser/connect, bearer mode): identity({refresh}), current(), listDevices(), discoveryKeys() and leave(), over the page's DeviceKeyPort (IndexedDB, non-extractable) and client-core peer/cert. The roster, certificate and K_disc are one pkey.connect.v1 record in the page's IndexedDB (memory with memory-only keys, which need allowEphemeralKeys); K_disc is non-enumerable and in no error. The previous K_disc goes 24 h after first seen, on roster loss or re-key and on leave; a 3.5-day short-circuit, which refresh bypasses; one call at a time; an unreadable record is an error that leave clears. Sign-out and deactivation call leave() and fail closed; a page without pinned keys answers the typed runtime N/A. The connect-identity* transcripts replay in test/transcripts.test.ts; test/connectIdentity.test.ts pins the rest.

connect.noise.note: client-core's peer/noise.ts over WebCrypto X25519 and AES-256-GCM, which the web relay sessions run (the DH of this device's key goes through DeviceKeyPort.dh); the browser runner drives every noise-vectors.json row in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (conformance/runners/browser/noiseVectors.browser.test.ts), and test/connectRelay.test.ts runs a full XXpsk0 admission between two devices.

connect.protocol.note: client-core's peer/ codecs (frame, record, relay, payload) and the PeerChannel session machine, which the web relay sessions run in mode a (test/connectRelay.test.ts: admission, 200 KB MORE reassembly, rekey-free close); the peer-matrix.json sections are driven by conformance/runners/node.

connect.lan.note: A browser or renderer has no sockets; the relay is its only path, and the host's Node SDK does the rest.

connect.relay.note: ui-core browser/connect (relay.ts, CC-09.2) behind adapter.cloudConnect and useCloudConnect(): connect.relayTicket() (the pkeyrt_ ticket, shape-checked, wss and the Worker's own host only; typed RelayError for relay_disabled, relay_paused with Retry-After capped at 3600 s, relay_quota_exceeded with its scope), a RelayService over the browser's WebSocket (pkey-relay.1, the ticket as the second subprotocol) with client-core's envelope codec, one PeerChannel per (peer, session) in the literal mode a (v and p never cross: assertRelayMode), backoff with jitter and a floor that resets only after 30 s stable, byte-capped session queues (peer_busy past 8 MiB; a WebSocket cannot be paused) and a bounded PeerDocs queue, a pushed RING through the identity replacement rules (keysStale, deferred refresh, one refresh a minute), a pushed TRUST verified against the usable pins with anti-rollback under the session's trust lock, and nothing secret reachable through JSON.stringify, enumerable fields or console. The relay code loads on the first start() (the React size budgets hold). The connect-relay-ticket and connect-relay-quota transcripts replay in test/transcripts.test.ts; test/connectRelay.test.ts pins the rest.

connect.links.note: A browser or renderer has no sockets; the relay is its only path, and the host's Node SDK does the rest. CC-19.9: <LinkPairing> and useLinkPairing draw the pairing window over a driver (linkPairingDriver(client.cloudConnect.links) of the host's Node SDK, or any LinkPairingDriver); the sockets and the contact store stay the host's.

connect.transfer.note: adapter.cloudConnect.transfer (ui-core browser/connect transfer.ts and xferStore.ts, CC-20.4; WIRE-CONTRACT-V5 §15.11), mode a over the relay only (a page cannot pair, D-14): send(peer, source, {name, type, chunk, signal, id, onStart}) for a device id or an open session, from a Blob (a File is one), a ReadableStream or bytes (streams are spooled and hashed first); onOffer(handler) decides each offer (no handler, a refusal, an error or an unusable sink declines; the answer is {blob}, {stream} or {file: FileSystemFileHandle}, so nothing downloads on its own); onResult(fn); cancel(id); maxSize; purge(). Sessions list xfer/1 by default; client-core's XferEndpoint runs the machine over ConnectSession.xferPort(). Partial transfers live in one IndexedDB database per product (named by the derived reference only; 24 h, 8 per peer, 64 in all, room from navigator.storage.estimate() set aside at the accept and enforced on each write), are removed on sign-out, deactivation and leave(), and reach the host's sink only after the hash matched. Only the tab that owns the relay session transfers; another tab's send is a LanError elsewhere. The engine loads with the relay on the first start() (the React size budgets hold). The peer-matrix xfer rows run in conformance/runners/browser/peerMatrix.browser.test.ts; test/connectTransfer.test.ts (@pkey-feature connect.transfer) is the two-session test over the relay fixture. CC-19.9: <TransferOffer> and useTransferOffer ship the D-8 consent prompt over a TransferOfferDriver.

connect.local.note: A browser or renderer has no sockets, and local links never use the relay; in Electron the host's Node SDK pairs and holds the links. CC-29K.1 draws the Pair with a Code screens over a driver.

connect.app.note: adapter.cloudConnect / useCloudConnect() (CC-09.2): start, stop, peers, refreshPeers, devices, open, onChannel, onNotice, status and onChange, with the relay as the only path (a page cannot discover devices on a LAN: connect.lan is the typed runtime N/A). A page without pinned keys and the local adapter answer the typed runtime N/A, the desktop renderer the version N/A (its host runs the Node SDK). Sign-out and deactivation stop it before leaving the roster.
